@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M0SVAZ3WJH2BQFJSA6E4X8NW
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9380'
+title: Give ShellRunner the command and environment caps that ShellPolicy owned
+---
+## What
+
+`Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Shell/ShellRunner.swift:287-291`
+says the limit on the length of the command and the limit on the length of an
+environment value *"belong to `ShellPolicy`, which the caller runs before this
+call. The runner takes input that is already examined."*
+
+`ShellPolicy` is deleted, thus **no layer examines either limit**. The runner
+states that its own one cap is `maxOutputSize`. An unbounded command string or
+environment value now reaches `posix_spawn`, where the operating system fails it
+with `E2BIG` far from the cause.
+
+This is not a doc edit. Give the runner the two caps, because it is now the last
+layer before the spawn:
+
+- Add a cap on the length of the command text and a cap on the length of one
+  environment value. Put both beside `maxOutputSize` in the same options type,
+  with the same shape, thus the runner has one place that holds its limits.
+- A command or a value over the cap gives a **corrective result in band**. It is
+  never thrown: eventplan.md § "Consolidation of the siblings" states that a
+  corrective result stays in band. The message names the cap and the measured
+  length.
+- Rewrite the doc at lines 287-291. It must state that the runner owns these
+  caps, and it must not name `ShellPolicy`.
+
+Read the sibling
+`../FoundationModelsShelltool/Sources/ShellTool/ShellPolicy.swift` for the two
+cap values it used, and keep those numbers unless they are plainly wrong.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `ShellRunner` holds a command-length cap and an environment-value-length
+      cap beside `maxOutputSize`.
+- [ ] A command over the cap gives a corrective result in band, never a throw.
+- [ ] An environment value over the cap gives a corrective result in band.
+- [ ] The corrective message names the cap and the measured length.
+- [ ] `ShellRunner.swift` names `ShellPolicy` nowhere.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] New cases in `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/ShellRunnerTests.swift`.
+- [ ] A test gives a command one byte over the cap and asserts the corrective
+      result, and that nothing was thrown.
+- [ ] A test gives a command exactly at the cap and asserts it runs.
+- [ ] A test gives an environment value over the cap and asserts the corrective
+      result.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter ShellRunner` passes.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes with no new failure and no new warning.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #phase-2 #eventplan
\ No newline at end of file

     Plan: `maximumCommandLengthBytes = 262_144` and `maximumEnvironmentValueLengthBytes = 1024` as named constants; an `EnvironmentValueDefect` enum carrying the three checks as data (a switch over a closed enum, which the `data-driven` rule states IS the table); one message shape that names the failed check, the cap and the measured byte length. `ShellRunner` is not touched.
   timestamp: 2026-08-24T21:20:18.067085+00:00
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m0ttjcbf9asnf08azv76zvfv
+  text: |-
+    Implementation landed, under TDD.
+
+    RED first: the six new cases were written before the code and the run failed with `type 'Execute' has no member 'maximumCommandLengthBytes'`. GREEN after: 19 cases in `ShellExecuteTests`, then 577 cases over 46 suites, all passing.
+
+    What the verb now holds, all in `Execute.swift`:
+
+    - `maximumCommandLengthBytes = 262_144` and `maximumEnvironmentValueLengthBytes = 1024`, both `internal` so a test can stand one byte over the cap and one byte under it without writing the number twice.
+    - `EnvironmentValueDefect`, a `CaseIterable` enum of the three ported checks — `.overLength`, `.embeddedNull`, `.embeddedLineBreak`. A closed enum switch IS the table the `data-driven` rule asks for, so the three checks are data rather than a chain of `if` statements.
+    - `commandTooLongCorrection(measuring:)` and `EnvironmentValueDefect.correction(forValueNamed:measuring:)`. One message shape for all three value defects, thus every message names the failed check, the cap AND the measured byte length.
+    - `environmentRefusal(in:)` reads the entries in the order of their names. A dictionary carries no order, and without the sort a map with two bad values would name a different one on each call, which reads as two mistakes.
+
